findings.detail: `IAiService.translateBatch` (types/ai.types.ts:16) and the standalone `translateBatch` (services/geminiService.ts:235) both gained `onNotice`, but the class wrapper did not — it still declares `options: { sourceLang; targetLang; domain; glossary }`. `GeminiService` is the ONLY implementation of `IAiService`, and it is what `aiServiceFactory.getService()` hands to `TranslateTab.tsx:286`, so this is the signature on the real call path. It compiles (TypeScript keeps method-syntax parameter bivariance even under `strict: true`) and it works at runtime only incidentally, because line 671 forwards `options` by reference rather than rebuilding it. Meanwhile all four new fallback tests (tests/unit/geminiModels.test.ts:198-230) import the standalone function directly, so nothing covers the wrapper. The concrete failure: someone later normalises the wrapper to `return translateBatch(items, { sourceLang, targetLang, domain, glossary })` — a change that looks like tidying and that the declared type actively invites — and every fallback notice is silently dropped. All four tests stay green, the workbook goes back to looking identical to one produced entirely on Pro, and ADR-0006's headline consequence ("A fallback is no longer silent") quietly becomes false again. Today there is no user impact; that is why this is medium and not high.
findings.summary: GeminiService wrapper never got `onNotice`; new tests bypass the path the app uses

findings.detail: The length-mismatch branch (line 309) logs that the whole batch was discarded and leaves `batchTranslated` at 0. The `if (batchTranslated < currentBatchItems.length)` check at line 334 is outside that if/else, so it fires immediately afterwards and logs "N item(s) in this batch came back empty — left untranslated." for a batch that did not come back empty — it came back misaligned and was deliberately thrown away. The user reading the log sees two error lines giving two different causes for one event, and the second one contradicts the first and points at the model rather than at the safety check that just did the right thing. This matters more than usual here because the log is the primary diagnostic for a PARTIAL run.
findings.summary: A discarded batch also logs a contradictory "came back empty" error

findings.detail: The comment states: `grep -rn "gemini-" components/` should stay empty. I ran it — it is not empty. `components/SupportChat.tsx:433` matches, on the historical comment "`ai.models.generateContent` with a hardcoded \"gemini-3-pro-preview\"". The substantive claim behind it is correct (no model id is *used* in `components/` any more), but the check as written fails on its first run. This PR's own commit history shows the cost of stale comments — two commits here exist partly to fix earlier comments that later commits falsified — so a self-checking invariant that does not actually pass is worth correcting now rather than becoming the third instance.
findings.summary: Docblock asserts an invariant that is false the moment it was written

findings.detail: Observation, not a request — line 295 predates this PR and is not in the diff. `return JSON.parse(response.text || "[]")` inside a function declared `Promise<string[]>` is an unvalidated assertion over model output, which is exactly why `TranslateTab.tsx:309` now has to defend with `!Array.isArray(translations) || translations.length !== currentBatchItems.length` against a value TypeScript insists is already `string[]`. The guard is correct and well-reasoned where it is, and TranslateTab is the right place for the *policy* decision (discard vs. partial-credit). Worth knowing: `extractStructuredData`, `extractFromMedia` and `processGeneralFile` parse model output the same way and have no equivalent guard, so the class of bug this PR fixed for Translate is still open for OCR, Compare and Web Scraper — and those callers map results positionally too. Raising this to a finding would require confirming those call sites actually index by position, which is outside this diff.
findings.summary: Shape validation landed in the caller; the other three parse sites still lack it
